hook: Which layout needs fewer removals over these requests?

The why applies the lesson's own model and limits (see this lesson's idea, limit and formula claims). Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. FC LH-3B (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED. The lesson model (formula: removals=(N-1)×uses at position N; the order view draws N items) gives 16 and 4 for N=5, but the question says only that "two bins share a cupboard 5 deep" and never states that anything sits between them. With only two bins, the back bin has one blocker, so "each of the 4 uses moves 4 blockers" does not follow and no option is right on a literal reading. Fix (example wording, owner decides): question "Two bins share a cupboard 5 deep, with 3 other boxes between the front and back positions: …", or the why "…each of the 4 uses moves the 4 items in front of it…" together with the question saying that the cupboard is full. See company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH3-2026-10-14.md (Batch B). Revised by demo-builder 2026-10-14 (W-389): question now states the fix (see recall-patch-home.lines.txt); status reset to unverified for fact-check re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Fresh instance under the W-280 ruling (the LH-3B dispute wording was adopted); I read HomeLesson.tsx and home-models.ts first. Question now states 3 boxes between the bins in a 5-deep cupboard: frequent at back, 4 uses x 4 blockers = 16; at front, only the rare use pays 4 = 4. Option '16 and 4' (index 0) unique; matches weighted-access (N - 1) x uses.

recall.question: Two bins sit at the front and back of a cupboard 5 deep, with 3 other boxes between them. You open one 4 times a season, the other once. With the frequent bin at the back, how many removals is that over the season, against having it at the front?
recall.why: At the back, each of the 4 uses moves 4 blockers (the 3 boxes and the other bin): 16. At the front, only the once-a-season request pays the 4: total 4. Count access cost across uses, not one retrieval. The frequencies are examples.
